clusters.name: Jonah leaving home for the conservatory, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around Jonah starting at Wexley Conservatory in September 1991, within months: a wrist injury that stopped his playing in October, a blow-up with his roommate Rafe who moved out that November, days high and absorbed in fixing radios, and by January 1992 feeling lost and low with no footing. His grandfather Gordon died in June 1991, and with his mother about to remarry, too much was moving at once. Every shift in these months is Jonah's own.

clusters.name: Jonah's burnout from performing and move away, 2001–2003
clusters.reason: Around September 2001 when Jonah began running out of steam for performing, within two years: his grandmother Winifred found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, a disastrous audition in early 2002 where he was done with performing, growing distance from family and friends by September 2002, a move to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone, a new partner Marisol met at a winter party in early 2003, a move to Fenwick to live with her by June 2003, a split within the year, and a deep depression that took hold once he returned to Thornbury that autumn. By late 2003 he was barely moving from the sofa; he relied on friends Silas, Corbin, and Dale rather than family. Every shift in these months is Jonah's own, and no one else's shows then.

clusters.name: Jonah's grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around January 2008 when Lorna died, within months: Jonah drained and withdrawn at Alder Creek in July, unable to manage a phone call with his mother, then keeping the door shut on her when she pressed to visit, and by August stopping all speech with her when he moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school. The silence held for roughly a year. Three shifts pile up in these months around the grandmother's death and the nursing school move.

clusters.name: Wren and Jonah's wedding, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around March 2017 when Jonah married Wren, contact with his mother eased off slightly. By October 2019, within months of Wren's mother's retirement party at the lake house: Wren swamped with one thing after another, Jonah overfunctioning laying out a strict plan to settle her, Wren's family fused in constant talk with her father and brother, Jonah awake from the small hours at the lake weekend unable to sleep and pulling back as others rose, and Wren anxious afterward on long quiet drives home. His sleep at its worst around her family; he feels he doesn't belong. Shifts pile up around the wedding and the lake weekend.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
